name: Air Medal (miniature medal body)
size_basis: estimated: the body measured in the Vanguard product photograph against the suspension ribbon's width, 262 px taken as 1.375 in (the full-size suspension ribbon, 1 3/8 in, DoDM 1348.33 as relayed in ASSET_NOTES.md and not verified in the repo): body 1.4747 x 1.6269 in in the photograph, halved for the miniature (DoDM 1348.33: miniature medals are one-half the size of the full-size medal). Height follows the body's own aspect. The width is the existing CAP asset's (0.625 in, assets/medals, kept as the brief asks; the photo measures 0.7374 in). The drawing keeps the width and the box; it is built from the photograph's own measured proportions (body scale 453.6 px per in, body width 0.625 in).
ribbon_attach_note: ribbon_attach is the bail axis at the box top (the box cuts the ring away) (upright body, hang angle 0 deg removed); compose.js hangs it at the drape's V point

frame.note: body width 0.625 in (the spec width) sets the scale; every length below is inches in the medal frame (origin = disc centre, +y down, UPRIGHT: the photograph is rotated by the measured hang angle into this frame)

measured.hang_angle_note: measured from the bail axis against the disc centre in the photograph (frame.js); the drawing hangs upright (bail and disc axis vertical)

inner_circle.note: dark rim line fitted on 15 angles (r 0.1815 to the line, 0.183 used for the edge)

not_measurable: The photograph shows a SIXTEEN-point sunburst (counted: 15 tips visible, the top tip is covered by the fleur-de-lis tails, tips every 22.5 deg, radius 0.310 to 0.316 in), not twelve points; the top spike is assumed the same as the other fifteen (its tip is hidden).

The top of the suspension ring is behind the ribbon in the photograph: only the lower arc (about 30 percent) is visible; the ring is drawn as the circle through that arc (r 0.099 in, centre v -0.519 in). The top end of the pendant is also under the ribbon; it is drawn up to v -0.465 in where the ribbon begins.

The two toes-and-claws of each foot are a tangle of five or six rounded knuckles round the bolt: drawn as six rounded lobes per foot (position and extent measured, the toe and claw separation is not resolved); claws are not drawn.

The bolts run under the feet and the tail: their upper ends are read at about (0.11, -0.05) and (0.19, -0.05) in from the visible parts; each dagger is modelled as a leaf-shaped blade (widest about 35 percent from the tip), the photograph shows a ridge along each blade that is not drawn.

Fan (far wing): the photograph shows about nine faint feather ridges, five are drawn; secondaries and covert feather lines on the lobes and on the back are only partly drawn (four lines on the back, none inside the lobes).

The eagle body, back and neck are flat tones with the groove lines the relief edges give; the photograph has smooth shading across them, engraving grain, dark pits and specular highlights, none drawn. The dark halo round the eagle is a flat band (0.013 in beyond the edge of the wing, 0.006 in at the shoulder), the photograph has a gradient 0.02 to 0.03 in wide.

The shared ribbon mask (ref.js) floods through every coloured pixel, so it takes this bronze body for ribbon; airmedal.js replaces it, for its own process only, with a blue and orange stripe mask (the silhouette gate then sees the body).

The existing box (0.625 x 0.6898 in miniature, 1.375 x 1.6706 in full) is kept: in the miniature the box top (v -0.377 in) lies just above the fleur-de-lis side petals and cuts the pendant; in the full body it cuts the pendant at v -0.447 in and shows only the lowest 0.03 in of the ring.

notes: Designed miniature medal body (LIVE13-ART 26). Measured from air-medal-full-size-medal.jpeg (reference only, never shipped). Air Medal: bronze sixteen-point sunburst with a recessed roundel holding a stooping eagle that clutches two lightning bolts, hung by a fleur-de-lis and a ring. Reference check: the photograph is the Air Medal (eagle, two bolts, fleur-de-lis), full size, in bronze; the same design serves the miniature. Hang angle 0 deg of the photograph removed: the body hangs upright.
